AnophelesModel.Rmd

Introduction

The AnophelesModel package parameterises a model of the mosquito feeding cycle (Chitnis, Smith, and Steketee 2008) using mosquito bionomics, human activity patterns, and user-supplied intervention efficacy parameters. It estimates the species-specific impact of vector control interventions on vectorial capacity and can generate parameterisations for OpenMalaria. Version 2 is a refactoring of version 1 and is not backward compatible (see NEWS.md for the differences).

The five feeding-cycle stages are: Host seeking → Host found (PAi) → Fed (PBi) → Resting (PCi) → Ovipositing (PDi) → back to Host seeking (PEi).

The typical analysis follows these steps:

  1. def_vector_params(), def_host_params() and def_activity_patterns() (with calculate_exposure())
  2. build_model_obj()
  3. build_intervention() (or get_ITN_params() for published ITN parameterisations)
  4. calculate_impact(), or run_interventions() for many scenarios and uncertainty draws
  5. optionally, export to OpenMalaria

Package database 

library(AnophelesModel)

Host parameters (host_ent_param): species-independent transition probabilities (PBi, PCi, PDi, PEi, Kvi) for human and animal hosts in the absence of interventions.

Mosquito bionomics (vec_ent_param): parameterisations for 57 Anopheles species, 17 complexes and the genus, from the AnophelesBionomics package, which estimates each parameter with a hierarchical Bayesian model (genus, complex, species) from published field data. Taxa are identified by their name and level (species, complex, genus); imputed_traits lists the parameters for which a taxon has no data of its own (values from its complex or the genus). The resting duration tau is estimated from the ratio of fed to gravid females in resting collections.

Activity patterns (activity_patterns): mosquito biting rhythms and human sleeping activity (Sherrard-Smith et al. 2019; Briët et al. 2019). Query with list_activity().

Estimating the impact of vector control interventions

Step 1: Define vector entomological parameters

Choose an existing taxon from the database. An. gambiae s.s. and An. coluzzii are merged in the data; “Anopheles gambiae” is also accepted for this species, with a warning:

gambiae_vec_p = def_vector_params(mosquito_species = "Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii")

A complex is selected with level = "complex" (e.g. the whole Gambiae complex). By default the human blood index Chi is the indoor HBI; hbi = "outdoor" or hbi = "weighted" (indoor and outdoor HBI weighted by endophagy) are alternatives:

gambiae_complex = def_vector_params("Gambiae", level = "complex")
gambiae_outdoor = def_vector_params("Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii", hbi = "outdoor")

A newer version of the bionomics table (same columns) can be used without reinstalling the package: def_vector_params(..., bionomics_table = read_bionomics_table("file.csv")).

Or supply a custom data frame with (a subset of) the column names of vec_ent_param. The model needs M (parous rate), Chi (human blood index, HBI), A0 (sac rate), zeta.3, td, tau (resting duration, days) and ts (extrinsic incubation period, a whole number of days); a missing or out-of-range value is an error. Chi is used as supplied:

custom_vec_table = data.frame(
    species_name  = "My species",
    M = 0.623, M.sd = 0.06,    # parous rate
    Chi = 0.939,                # Human Blood Index (HBI)
    A0 = 0.313, A0.sd = 0.03,  # sac rate
    zeta.3 = 1, td = 0.33, tau = 1.1, ts = 10, to = 5,
    endophily = 0.813, endophily.sd = 0.07,
    endophagy = 0.813, endophagy.sd = 0.07
)
custom_vec_p = def_vector_params(vector_table = custom_vec_table)

Step 2: Define host-specific parameters

Host parameters are defined as follows:

host_p = def_host_params()
print(host_p)
#> $species_name
#> [1] "Anopheles gambiae" "Anopheles gambiae"
#> 
#> $host
#> [1] "human"  "animal"
#> 
#> $PBi
#> [1] 0.95 0.95
#> 
#> $PCi
#> [1] 0.95 0.95
#> 
#> $PDi
#> [1] 0.99 0.99
#> 
#> $PEi
#> [1] 0.88 0.88
#> 
#> $Kvi
#> [1] 0.03 0.00

A custom table (one human and one animal row, probabilities in [0, 1]) can be passed via host_table:

custom_host_table = data.frame(
    host = c("human", "animal"),
    PBi = c(0.95, 0.70), PCi = c(0.90, 0.70),
    PDi = c(0.90, 0.80), PEi = c(0.88, 0.80),
    Kvi = c(0.52, 0.00)
)
custom_host_p = def_host_params(host_table = custom_host_table)

Step 3: Define activity patterns and compute exposure

Use the built-in defaults or select from the database by entry ID:

# Built-in default (An. gambiae, Kenya)
activity_gambiae = def_activity_patterns("default_Anopheles_gambiae")

# From database by entry ID
activity_arabiensis = def_activity_patterns(list(
    HBI = 34, HBO = 165, humans_indoors = 4, humans_in_bed = 24
))

Time-series vectors can also be supplied directly as a named list with elements HBI, HBO, humans_indoors, humans_in_bed.

calculate_exposure() decomposes total human exposure into indoor/outdoor components. For example, Exposure_Indoor_whileinbed gives the fraction of bites received indoors while sleeping — the portion an ITN would protect against (for IRS, see below). Unlike in version 1, exposure does not modify the intervention efficacies: it reduces the effective coverage (coverage × exposure), passed via the exposure argument of calculate_impact() and run_interventions():

exposure = calculate_exposure(activity_cycles = activity_gambiae,
                              vec_p           = gambiae_vec_p)
print(exposure)
#> $Exposure_Indoor_total
#> [1] 0.9415679
#> 
#> $Exposure_Outdoor_total
#> [1] 0.0584321
#> 
#> $Exposure_Indoor_whileinbed
#> [1] 0.9238849
#> 
#> $Exposure_Outdoor_whileinbed
#> [1] 0.01055327
#> 
#> $indoor_resting
#> [1] 0.7258244

Which mosquitoes does IRS reach? Two choices are defensible, and the package offers both:

  • mosquitoes resting indoors (indoor_resting, the endophily): spraying reaches the mosquitoes resting on the walls;
  • mosquitoes biting indoors (Exposure_Indoor_total): the share of bites received indoors, where IRS is deployed.

They agree only when the share of mosquitoes resting indoors equals the share of bites indoors. Neither is wrong in itself; the appropriate one depends on how the IRS efficacies were estimated. Use the same choice in the vectorial capacity calculation and in the OpenMalaria export:

  • here, pass exposure = exposure$indoor_resting or exposure = exposure$Exposure_Indoor_total to calculate_impact() / run_interventions();
  • in the OpenMalaria export, get_OM_ento_snippet(irs_exposure = "indoor_resting") (default) or "indoor_biting" (see “Export to OpenMalaria”).

Step 4: Build the model object 

model_p = build_model_obj(gambiae_vec_p, host_p)
print(model_p$host_params$muvA)    # mosquito death rate while host-seeking
#> [1] 0.6461614
print(model_p$host_params$alphai)  # per-individual-host availability rates
#> [1] 1.9794421 0.3109918

Step 5: Build an intervention object

Efficacy parameters map directly to feeding-cycle probabilities:

Parameter Mechanism Model
Deterrency Reduces host availability (alphai) for protected humans: deterred mosquitoes keep searching Both
PrePrandial Kills mosquitoes after they find a protected human, before they feed: reduces the probability of biting and surviving (PBi) Standard (3 hosts)
PostPrandial Kills mosquitoes after feeding: reduces the probability of surviving to find a resting place (PCi) Both
KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute Adds a dummy host: mosquitoes killed while searching Dummy-host (4 hosts)

In the feeding-cycle model, a mosquito that fails a stage after finding a host dies, so pre- and post-prandial effects are mortality.

Any subset of the components can be given (omitted ones are 0). Deterrency, PrePrandial and PostPrandial are probabilities in [0, 1]. In the dummy-host model, KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute replaces PrePrandial (a non-zero PrePrandial with it is an error): mosquitoes are killed while searching for a host, through a fourth “dummy” host whose availability is KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute. As the name says, it is an absolute rate (per day, in the units of the host availabilities alphai), not a probability, and can exceed 1. By a provisional convention, the per hut-night rates of experimental hut fits are used as per-day rates.

All components share an attrition decay (halflife_attrition, shape_attrition, decay_attrition) describing physical degradation over time. The decay function (decay_attrition) is one of those of OpenMalaria: "weibull", "exponential", "hill", "linear", "step", "smooth-compact" and "none". Its parameter L (halflife_attrition) is the half-life (value 0.5 at t = L) for Weibull, exponential and Hill, and the time at which the effect reaches zero for linear, step and smooth-compact. The shape parameter kappa (shape_attrition) is needed for Weibull, Hill and smooth-compact. All these decay functions start at 1 and decrease towards 0, so the efficacy never exceeds its initial value (the only exception is a negative halflife_insecticide, see below).

#> Warning: package 'ggplot2' was built under R version 4.5.3

Decay functions (L=365 days, kappa=2 where applicable).

Built-in ITN parameterisations. list_ITN_params() lists the nets and experimental hut trials (EHT) of the database (Champagne et al. 2025), each available for both model structures; the net type (net_type) and the EHT are the arguments of get_ITN_params():

head(list_ITN_params())
#>           netType         EHT                     reference
#> 1  Interceptor G2     Assenga      Assenga et al., Tanzania
#> 2     Olyset Plus     Assenga      Assenga et al., Tanzania
#> 3 Pyrethroid-only     Assenga      Assenga et al., Tanzania
#> 4  Interceptor G2 Assenga, CI Assenga et al., Côte d'Ivoire
#> 5     Olyset Plus Assenga, CI Assenga et al., Côte d'Ivoire
#> 6 Pyrethroid-only Assenga, CI Assenga et al., Côte d'Ivoire

Standard model — built-in parameterisation for Interceptor G2 from the Kibondo EHT, with Weibull attrition (half-life 3 years) and per-component linear insecticide decay, passed via halflife_insecticide (in years). Despite its name, this is the time at which the effect would reach zero, calibrated so that the efficacy at the aging time of the trial’s washed arm (3 years, 2 for Sovegnon) equals the efficacy of nets washed 20 times (a negative value, when washed nets perform better, makes the effect increase over time):

itn_p = get_ITN_params("Interceptor G2", "Kibondo")
#> ITN parameterisation loaded: Interceptor G2 (Kibondo) 
#> Mode: standard 
#> Reference: Kibondo et al. 
#> Efficacy (unwashed):
#> PostPrandial  PrePrandial   Deterrency 
#>         0.52         0.44         0.71 
#> Insecticide decay, linear time to zero (years; omitted = no decay):
#> PostPrandial  PrePrandial   Deterrency 
#>         31.2         66.0        -71.0

my_interv = build_intervention(
    efficacy             = itn_p$efficacy,
    halflife_insecticide = itn_p$halflife_insecticide,
    mode                 = itn_p$mode,
    halflife_attrition =  3*365, shape_attrition = 2, decay_attrition = "weibull",
    duration_years = 3, model_p = model_p, name = itn_p$name
)
#> build_intervention: using standard (3-host) model with PrePrandial.

With insecticide decay (the default insecticide_decay = TRUE), the object also contains, for each efficacy component, the single Weibull decay that best approximates attrition × insecticide decay (as used for OpenMalaria GVI parameterisations). The model itself uses the exact decay:

my_interv[[1]]$fitted_decay
#>      component        L    kappa        rmse
#> 1   Deterrency 1123.920 2.111902 0.001447042
#> 2  PrePrandial 1061.447 1.899377 0.001289616
#> 3 PostPrandial 1021.847 1.806974 0.002467478

Set insecticide_decay = FALSE to ignore the insecticide decay and keep the unwashed efficacy throughout (only attrition decays):

my_interv_nodecay = build_intervention(
    efficacy = itn_p$efficacy, halflife_insecticide = itn_p$halflife_insecticide,
    mode = itn_p$mode, insecticide_decay = FALSE,
    halflife_attrition = 3*365, shape_attrition = 2, decay_attrition = "weibull",
    duration_years = 3, model_p = model_p, name = itn_p$name
)

Custom efficacy values can also be supplied directly:

my_interv_custom = build_intervention(
    efficacy = c(Deterrency = 0.50, PrePrandial = 0.60, PostPrandial = 0.70),
    halflife_attrition = 3*365, shape_attrition = 2, decay_attrition = "weibull",
    duration_years = 3, model_p = model_p, name = "Custom ITN"
)

Dummy-host model — host-seeking killing replaces pre-prandial; deterrency and post-prandial killing remain. Use mode = "dummy_host" to load the corresponding parameters from the database. In the hut trial fits, host-seeking killing is estimated relative to the availability alpha_0 of the trial’s control arm (KillingDuringHostSeekingRelative in the database); since alpha_0 varies widely between trials, get_ITN_params() multiplies it back by the control alpha_0 of the same arm (unwashed or washed) to return the absolute value KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute, comparable across trials and used by the model (rescale_hsk = FALSE returns the relative value, e.g. to rescale it with another alpha_0; the model does not accept it):

itn_dh_p = get_ITN_params("Interceptor G2", "Kibondo", mode = "dummy_host")
#> ITN parameterisation loaded: Interceptor G2 (Kibondo) 
#> Mode: dummy_host 
#> Reference: Kibondo et al. 
#> Efficacy (unwashed):
#>                     PostPrandial                       Deterrency 
#>                            0.520                            0.710 
#> KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute 
#>                            0.609 
#> Host-seeking killing rescaled by the control alpha_0 (unwashed 0.17, washed 0.16)
#> Insecticide decay, linear time to zero (years; omitted = no decay):
#>                     PostPrandial                       Deterrency 
#>                           31.200                          -71.000 
#> KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute 
#>                           28.981

my_interv_dh = build_intervention(
    efficacy             = itn_dh_p$efficacy,
    halflife_insecticide = itn_dh_p$halflife_insecticide,
    mode                 = itn_dh_p$mode,
    halflife_attrition = 180, shape_attrition = 2, decay_attrition = "weibull",
    duration_years = 3, model_p = model_p, name = itn_dh_p$name
)
#> build_intervention: using dummy-host (4-host) model with KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute.
# effects matrices now have 4 columns (protected humans, unprotected, animals, dummy host)
ncol(my_interv_dh[[1]]$effects$alphai)
#> [1] 4

Per-component decay — each efficacy component can decay independently via the component_decay argument (optional: when absent, a component stays at its initial value throughout and only the attrition decay applies):

my_interv_compdecay = build_intervention(
    efficacy = c(Deterrency = 0.50, PrePrandial = 0.60, PostPrandial = 0.70),
    halflife_attrition = 365, shape_attrition = 2, decay_attrition = "weibull",
    duration_years = 3, model_p = model_p,
    name = "ITN (per-component decay)",
    component_decay = list(                           # optional per-component decay
        Deterrency  = list(decay = "hill",   L = 90,  kappa = 3),   # fast
        PrePrandial = list(decay = "linear", L = 730, kappa = NULL)  # slow
    )
)
#> build_intervention: using standard (3-host) model with PrePrandial.

Step 6: Calculate impact

Pass the intervention objects to calculate_impact() with the deployment coverages. For an ITN, the protected share of exposure is the in-bed exposure from Step 3; the model then uses the effective coverage coverage × exposure, while results are reported against deployment coverage. Several interventions are evaluated in one call: combine them with c() (not list(), since each build_intervention() output is already a list). Here, two standard-model ITNs of Step 5 (dummy-host interventions can be mixed in the same call):

coverages = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)

impacts = calculate_impact(
    interventions_vec = c(my_interv, my_interv_compdecay),
    coverage_vec      = coverages,
    model_p           = model_p,
    exposure          = exposure$Exposure_Indoor_whileinbed
)

The result is a table with one row per intervention and coverage: the intervention’s position and name, its parameters, then coverage, exposure, the average vectorial capacity avg_vc and its average reduction avg_impact over the duration of the intervention:

impacts[abs(impacts$coverage - 0.8) < 1e-9, c("name", "coverage", "avg_impact")]
#>                         name coverage avg_impact
#>                       <char>    <num>      <num>
#> 1:  Interceptor G2 (Kibondo)      0.8  0.8322229
#> 2: ITN (per-component decay)      0.8  0.5422930

plot_impact() draws one line per intervention, labelled with its name (give each intervention a distinct name, otherwise they share the label "custom"):

plot_impact(impacts, title = "Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii")
#> Ignoring unknown labels:
#> • fill : ""

Vectorial capacity reduction for two ITNs of Step 5.

With keep_time = TRUE, calculate_impact() also returns the vectorial capacity and its reduction on each day ($time), e.g. to follow the decay of the impact after deployment.

Step 7: Many scenarios and uncertainty with run_interventions()

run_interventions() takes the interventions as a table instead of objects: each row of a data frame param_sets is one intervention, and all rows are evaluated at all coverages in one call. calculate_impact() is run_interventions() applied to the parameters stored in each intervention object, so both give the same results, in the same format, and plot_impact() draws both.

  • Columns of param_sets: the efficacies deterrency, preprandial, postprandial (required) and optionally killing_during_host_seeking_absolute; the attrition decay decay_attrition (required), with halflife_attrition (days) unless it is "none" and shape_attrition for Weibull, Hill and smooth-compact; optional per-component decay columns (below). Any other column (e.g. name) is carried to the output.
  • Other arguments: coverage_vec, duration_years, exposure (as in calculate_impact()), and insecticide_decay = FALSE to ignore the per-component decay columns.
  • Output: a data.table with one row per parameter set and coverage (and draw): the input columns, then coverage, exposure, avg_vc and avg_impact.

Scenario sweep 

param_sets = data.frame(
    name         = c("Low efficacy", "Medium efficacy", "High efficacy"),
    deterrency   = c(0.20, 0.4, 0.5),
    preprandial  = c(0.25, 0.55, 0.80),
    postprandial = c(0.20, 0.50, 0.75),
    halflife_attrition = 180, shape_attrition = 2, decay_attrition = "weibull",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

results = run_interventions(
    param_sets   = param_sets,
    model_p      = model_p,
    coverage_vec = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2),
    duration_years = 3
)
#> run_interventions: using standard (3-host) model.
head(results)
#>            name deterrency preprandial postprandial halflife_attrition
#>          <char>      <num>       <num>        <num>              <num>
#> 1: Low efficacy        0.2        0.25          0.2                180
#> 2: Low efficacy        0.2        0.25          0.2                180
#> 3: Low efficacy        0.2        0.25          0.2                180
#> 4: Low efficacy        0.2        0.25          0.2                180
#> 5: Low efficacy        0.2        0.25          0.2                180
#> 6: Low efficacy        0.2        0.25          0.2                180
#>    shape_attrition decay_attrition coverage exposure    avg_vc avg_impact
#>              <num>          <char>    <num>    <num>     <num>      <num>
#> 1:               2         weibull      0.0        1 0.1919267 0.00000000
#> 2:               2         weibull      0.2        1 0.1759770 0.08310308
#> 3:               2         weibull      0.4        1 0.1648712 0.14096773
#> 4:               2         weibull      0.6        1 0.1569808 0.18207920
#> 5:               2         weibull      0.8        1 0.1512451 0.21196440
#> 6:               2         weibull      1.0        1 0.1469672 0.23425341
plot_impact(results)
#> Ignoring unknown labels:
#> • fill : ""

Vectorial capacity reduction for three efficacy scenarios.

Dummy-host model

The two model structures of Step 5 are mutually exclusive within a param_sets table. For the dummy-host model, add killing_during_host_seeking_absolute (an absolute rate, see Step 5) and set preprandial to 0 (the column stays required):

dummyhost_ps = data.frame(
    name         = c("Dummy-host ITN", "Dummy-host ITN, HSK decay"),
    deterrency   = 0.55,
    preprandial  = 0,
    postprandial = 0.24,
    killing_during_host_seeking_absolute = 1.10,
    halflife_attrition = 180, shape_attrition = 2, decay_attrition = "weibull",
    # second row: Weibull insecticide decay of host-seeking killing (half-life 90 days)
    decay_hsk = c(NA, "weibull"), L_hsk = c(NA, 90), kappa_hsk = c(NA, 2),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
res_dh = run_interventions(dummyhost_ps, model_p, seq(0, 1, by = 0.2),
                           duration_years = 3)
#> run_interventions: using dummy-host (4-host) model (killing_during_host_seeking_absolute column detected).
res_dh[, c("name", "coverage", "avg_impact")]
#>                          name coverage avg_impact
#>                        <char>    <num>      <num>
#>  1:            Dummy-host ITN      0.0 0.00000000
#>  2:            Dummy-host ITN      0.2 0.13790022
#>  3:            Dummy-host ITN      0.4 0.20723053
#>  4:            Dummy-host ITN      0.6 0.24649899
#>  5:            Dummy-host ITN      0.8 0.27140889
#>  6:            Dummy-host ITN      1.0 0.28883740
#>  7: Dummy-host ITN, HSK decay      0.0 0.00000000
#>  8: Dummy-host ITN, HSK decay      0.2 0.08415098
#>  9: Dummy-host ITN, HSK decay      0.4 0.13182898
#> 10: Dummy-host ITN, HSK decay      0.6 0.16254908
#> 11: Dummy-host ITN, HSK decay      0.8 0.18454659
#> 12: Dummy-host ITN, HSK decay      1.0 0.20157910

Per-component insecticide decay

As with halflife_insecticide and component_decay in build_intervention(), each efficacy can decay on top of attrition, with optional columns per component (suffix _det, _pre, _post, _hsk):

  • halflife_<suffix>: linear decay, time to zero in years;
  • decay_<suffix>, L_<suffix> (days), kappa_<suffix>: any decay function, overriding halflife_<suffix>.

NA or an absent column means no insecticide decay for that component:

# Three scenarios with identical initial efficacy but different component decays
comp_decay_ps = data.frame(
    name         = c("No comp. decay", "Fast deterrency", "Differential decay"),
    deterrency   = 0.55,
    preprandial  = 0.45,
    postprandial = 0.40,
    halflife_attrition = 365, shape_attrition = 2, decay_attrition = "weibull",
    # Scenario 2: deterrency decays fast (Weibull, half-life 60 d, kappa 3)
    # Scenario 3: deterrency fast (Weibull), pre-prandial slow (linear, 2 yr), post-prandial medium (linear, 1 yr)
    decay_det  = c(NA,        "weibull", "weibull"),
    L_det      = c(NA,         60,        60),
    kappa_det  = c(NA,          3,         3),
    decay_pre  = c(NA,        NA,        "linear"),
    L_pre      = c(NA,        NA,         730),
    kappa_pre  = c(NA,        NA,         NA),
    decay_post = c(NA,        NA,        "linear"),
    L_post     = c(NA,        NA,         365),
    kappa_post = c(NA,        NA,         NA),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

comp_results = run_interventions(
    param_sets   = comp_decay_ps,
    model_p      = model_p,
    coverage_vec = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),
    duration_years = 3
)
#> run_interventions: using standard (3-host) model.
head(comp_results[, c("name", "coverage", "avg_impact")])
#>              name coverage avg_impact
#>            <char>    <num>      <num>
#> 1: No comp. decay      0.0 0.00000000
#> 2: No comp. decay      0.1 0.09892436
#> 3: No comp. decay      0.2 0.18159449
#> 4: No comp. decay      0.3 0.25061732
#> 5: No comp. decay      0.4 0.30822350
#> 6: No comp. decay      0.5 0.35631635

Parameter uncertainty

Uncertainty is propagated with draws, supplied through up to four arguments. They are zipped: draw d uses entry d of every source supplied, so all must have the same number of draws. The output gains a draw column.

Argument One draw is Replaces
vec_param_sets a row with the columns of vec_ent_param the bionomics of model_p
interv_param_sets a row with the columns of param_sets param_sets
coverage_sets a vector of coverages (list element) coverage_vec
exposure_sets an exposure factor, e.g. from calculate_exposure() exposure

Vector bionomics. The database stores posterior means and standard deviations (M.sd, A0.sd, Chi.sd, tau.sd, …), but draws are not generated automatically. Here, 200 independent normal draws of the parous and sac rates of An. gambiae ss/coluzzii, truncated to (0, 1), which ignores correlations between parameters:

set.seed(42)
n_draws  = 200
base_vec = vec_ent_param[vec_ent_param$species_name == "Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii" &
                             vec_ent_param$level == "species", ]

vec_draws = base_vec[rep(1, n_draws), ]
vec_draws$M  = pmax(pmin(rnorm(n_draws, base_vec$M,  base_vec$M.sd),  0.999), 0.001)
vec_draws$A0 = pmax(pmin(rnorm(n_draws, base_vec$A0, base_vec$A0.sd), 0.999), 0.001)

single_scenario = data.frame(
    name="Medium efficacy ITN", deterrency=0.45, preprandial=0.55,
    postprandial=0.50, halflife_attrition=180, shape_attrition=2,
    decay_attrition="weibull", stringsAsFactors=FALSE
)
coverage_grid = seq(0, 1, by=0.1)

uncertainty_results = run_interventions(
    param_sets=single_scenario, model_p=model_p, coverage_vec=coverage_grid,
    vec_param_sets=vec_draws, duration_years=3
)
#> run_interventions: using standard (3-host) model.
# The draw-specific bionomics are included in the output
head(uncertainty_results)

# With draws, plot_impact() shows the median and the 95% interval
plot_impact(uncertainty_results, title = "200 draws of M and A0")

Uncertainty band (median + 95% interval) across 200 draws of vector parameters.

Across taxa. The same argument evaluates one intervention for many taxa: each row of vec_ent_param is then a “draw”, identified in the output by species_name and level. Filter on level (complexes and the genus have their own rows; a species alone in its complex is listed once, as a species). A taxon whose bionomics are inconsistent with the host parameters stops the run with an error:

all_species = vec_ent_param[vec_ent_param$level == "species", ]
res_species = run_interventions(single_scenario, model_p, coverage_vec = 0.8,
                                vec_param_sets = all_species, duration_years = 3)

Intervention parameters. Each row of interv_param_sets replaces param_sets for its draw:

set.seed(7)
n_draws_interv = 50
interv_draws = data.frame(
    name         = "ITN",
    deterrency   = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_draws_interv, 0.45, 0.08), 0), 1),
    preprandial  = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_draws_interv, 0.55, 0.10), 0), 1),
    postprandial = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_draws_interv, 0.50, 0.09), 0), 1),
    halflife_attrition = 180, shape_attrition = 2, decay_attrition = "weibull"
)

interv_unc_results = run_interventions(
    param_sets=single_scenario, model_p=model_p, coverage_vec=coverage_grid,
    interv_param_sets=interv_draws, duration_years=3
)
#> run_interventions: using standard (3-host) model.
nrow(interv_unc_results)   # 11 coverages x 50 draws
#> [1] 550

Several sources together, here 30 draws of both bionomics and intervention parameters:

n_draws_joint = 30
joint_results = run_interventions(
    param_sets=single_scenario, model_p=model_p, coverage_vec=coverage_grid,
    vec_param_sets    = vec_draws[seq_len(n_draws_joint), ],
    interv_param_sets = interv_draws[seq_len(n_draws_joint), ],
    duration_years=3
)
#> run_interventions: using standard (3-host) model.
nrow(joint_results)        # 11 coverages x 30 draws
#> [1] 330

Step 8: Combining two interventions

calculate_combined_impact() evaluates two interventions deployed together (e.g. ITN and IRS), given the coverage of each and the share of people covered by both (cov_combination, by default the product of the two coverages, i.e. independent deployment). For people covered by both, the effects combine multiplicatively, and host-seeking killing of dummy-host interventions adds up. The interventions are evaluated over the shorter of their two durations. There is no exposure argument, because the exposures of two interventions overlap (e.g. bites in bed are also indoor bites): pass exposure-adjusted coverages if needed.

interv_ITN = build_intervention(
    efficacy = c(Deterrency = 0.5, PrePrandial = 0.6, PostPrandial = 0.7),
    halflife_attrition = 180, shape_attrition = 2, decay_attrition = "weibull",
    duration_years = 1, model_p = model_p, name = "ITN"
)
#> build_intervention: using standard (3-host) model with PrePrandial.
interv_IRS = build_intervention(
    efficacy = c(Deterrency = 0.0, PrePrandial = 0.3, PostPrandial = 0.8),
    halflife_attrition = 180, shape_attrition = 2, decay_attrition = "weibull",
    duration_years = 1, model_p = model_p, name = "IRS"
)
#> build_intervention: using standard (3-host) model with PrePrandial.
combined_impact = calculate_combined_impact(
    combination_name  = "ITN + IRS",
    intervention1     = interv_ITN[[1]], intervention2 = interv_IRS[[1]],
    cov_intervention1 = 0.8,            cov_intervention2 = 0.8,
    model_p = model_p
)
#> ITN + IRS: assigned coverages 0.04 0.16 0.16 0.64
cat("Combined VC reduction:", round(combined_impact * 100, 1), "%\n")
#> Combined VC reduction: 88.1 %

Export to OpenMalaria

This section can be read on its own: it only uses the objects it creates.

OpenMalaria scenarios (schema 44 by default; dummy-host nets need schema 46 or later, see below) are written with openMalariaUtilities, which builds a scenario as an R list (baseList) and writes the XML file. This package does not write scenarios: it fills in the entomology and the vector control interventions of a baseList; the rest of the scenario (demography, health system, monitoring, …) and the XML file are produced with openMalariaUtilities, as usual. The steps are:

  1. get_OM_ento_snippet(): mosquito populations and their parameters;
  2. define_OM_entomology(): writes them into the baseList;
  3. om_vector_control(): specifies an ITN or IRS intervention;
  4. define_OM_vector_control() and deploy_OM_vector_control(): write its definition and its deployment.

openMalariaUtilities is not on CRAN and is only a suggested dependency: get_OM_ento_snippet(), om_vector_control(), om_scenario_values() and get_OM_xml() (XML text, see the end of this section) work without it, but define_OM_entomology() and define_OM_vector_control() require it. Install it from GitHub:

remotes::install_github("SwissTPH/r-openMalariaUtilities")

Entomology

Mosquito populations. get_OM_ento_snippet() gives the parameters of each species, from the bionomics database. With activity patterns, each species is split into three populations by the interventions that reach them: _indoor1 (reached by ITNs and IRS), _indoor2 (by only one of the two) and _outdoor (by neither). ITNs reach the mosquitoes biting in bed; IRS reaches those resting indoors (default) or, with irs_exposure = "indoor_biting", those biting indoors. In the latter case the split follows directly from the bites: _indoor1 is the share of bites in bed, _indoor2 the share of bites indoors outside bed; with resting indoors, the overlap of the two groups is assumed to be the largest possible. The populations share all parameters except the human blood index (indoor HBI for the indoor populations, outdoor HBI for the outdoor one). A population with a share of 0 (e.g. _indoor2 when the two groups are the same size) is not written. Without activity patterns, each species is a single population that ITNs and IRS reach entirely, outdoor bites included; the vector control export then gives a warning.

Contribution of each population to the EIR. The annualEIR of each population is its relative contribution to the EIR: the share of its species × its share within the species, summing to 1 over all populations. OpenMalaria rescales them to the total EIR, given separately in the scaledAnnualEIR attribute of <entomology> (a number or a placeholder such as "@EIR@"). The share of a species is its relative abundance weighted by its sporozoite rate, computed by eir_shares() (both are setting-specific; the values below are illustrative). The contributions are either:

  • fixed: pass the species shares as species_shares, and the contributions are written as numbers;
  • placeholders: leave out species_shares; each population then has a placeholder @contrib_<population>@, and om_ento_values() gives their values for one or several species compositions (one row each), e.g. to loop scenarios over species mixes.

Fixed contributions:

library(AnophelesModel)

spz = c("Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii" = 0.114, "Anopheles funestus" = 0.235)
mix = eir_shares(c("Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii" = 0.7, "Anopheles funestus" = 0.3), spz)
mix
#> Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii            Anopheles funestus 
#>                     0.5309381                     0.4690619

activity = def_activity_patterns("default_Anopheles_gambiae")
om_ento = get_OM_ento_snippet(names(mix), activity = activity, species_shares = mix)
#> get_OM_ento_snippet: annualEIR = the relative contribution of each population; set the total EIR with scaledAnnualEIR (e.g. defineEntomology(..., scaledAnnualEIR = "@EIR@")).
om_ento$shares
#>                                mosquito                         taxon    type
#> 1 Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii_indoor1 Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii indoor1
#> 2 Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii_indoor2 Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii indoor2
#> 3 Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii_outdoor Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii outdoor
#> 4            Anopheles funestus_indoor1            Anopheles funestus indoor1
#> 5            Anopheles funestus_indoor2            Anopheles funestus indoor2
#> 6            Anopheles funestus_outdoor            Anopheles funestus outdoor
#>        share in_bed indoor_resting       muvA species_share  eir_share
#> 1 0.72582440   TRUE           TRUE 0.64616143     0.5309381 0.38536784
#> 2 0.19806053   TRUE          FALSE 0.64616143     0.5309381 0.10515789
#> 3 0.07611507  FALSE          FALSE 0.64616143     0.5309381 0.04041239
#> 4 0.67730324   TRUE           TRUE 0.08629624     0.4690619 0.31769713
#> 5 0.24054877   TRUE          FALSE 0.08629624     0.4690619 0.11283226
#> 6 0.08214799  FALSE          FALSE 0.08629624     0.4690619 0.03853249

shares gives, per population, its share within the species (share), the share of its species (species_share), its share of the EIR (eir_share), whether ITNs (in_bed) or IRS (indoor_resting) reach it, and the host-seeking death rate muvA.

Placeholder contributions, and their values for two compositions (the columns contrib_<population> fill the placeholders of the same name):

om_ento_ph = get_OM_ento_snippet(names(mix), activity = activity)
#> get_OM_ento_snippet: annualEIR = a placeholder @contrib_<population>@ for the relative contribution of each population (values: om_ento_values()); set the total EIR with scaledAnnualEIR (e.g. defineEntomology(..., scaledAnnualEIR = "@EIR@")).
om_ento_ph$seasonalityParameters[[1]]$annualEIR
#> [1] "@contrib_Anopheles_gambiae_ss_coluzzii_indoor1@"
om_ento_values(om_ento_ph, rbind(mix = mix, equal = c(0.5, 0.5)))
#>   composition Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii Anopheles funestus
#> 1         mix                     0.5309381          0.4690619
#> 2       equal                     0.5000000          0.5000000
#>   contrib_Anopheles_gambiae_ss_coluzzii_indoor1
#> 1                                     0.3853678
#> 2                                     0.3629122
#>   contrib_Anopheles_gambiae_ss_coluzzii_indoor2
#> 1                                    0.10515789
#> 2                                    0.09903027
#>   contrib_Anopheles_gambiae_ss_coluzzii_outdoor
#> 1                                    0.04041239
#> 2                                    0.03805753
#>   contrib_Anopheles_funestus_indoor1 contrib_Anopheles_funestus_indoor2
#> 1                          0.3176971                          0.1128323
#> 2                          0.3386516                          0.1202744
#>   contrib_Anopheles_funestus_outdoor
#> 1                         0.03853249
#> 2                         0.04107400

Writing the entomology. define_OM_entomology() writes the entomology into the baseList, with the total EIR in scaledAnnualEIR (here a placeholder) and the seasonality, which gives the shape of the EIR over the year (OpenMalaria rescales it to the annual EIR). The baseList also keeps the entomology, so that the interventions use the same mosquito populations and parameters. The seasonality is either fixed numbers, or placeholders (default @m1@, …, @m12@, filled per scenario by columns m1, …, m12), which need a recent openMalariaUtilities (older versions reject them with R >= 4.3):

# baseList: an openMalariaUtilities scenario
baseList = define_OM_entomology(baseList, om_ento,
                                seasonality = c(2, 3, 5, 8, 6, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2),
                                scaledAnnualEIR = "@EIR@")
# or with the seasonality per scenario (columns m1..m12)
baseList = define_OM_entomology(baseList, om_ento, scaledAnnualEIR = "@EIR@")

Vector control

Specifying an intervention. om_vector_control() takes the efficacies of an intervention and its decays (attrition, and optionally insecticide decay), with no model or duration: the export builds the intervention with the entomology of the scenario, over the right period. It takes a built-in parameterisation from get_ITN_params() (see list_ITN_params() for the available nets and trials), or custom efficacies:

# Built-in: Interceptor G2, Kibondo hut trial, standard model
ig2 = om_vector_control(get_ITN_params("Interceptor G2", "Kibondo", verbose = FALSE),
                        halflife_attrition = 2 * 365, shape_attrition = 2)
# Custom
custom = om_vector_control(c(Deterrency = 0.4, PrePrandial = 0.5, PostPrandial = 0.3),
                           halflife_attrition = 2 * 365, shape_attrition = 2,
                           name = "Custom ITN")

Campaign schedules. om_campaigns() builds the schedule of campaigns: dates (regular, with from, to and every, or given) and coverages (numbers or placeholders such as "@cov2021@", one per year with by_year = TRUE):

om_campaigns(dates = c("2021-01-01", "2024-01-01"), coverage = c(0.8, 0.6))
#>         date coverage
#> 1 2021-01-01      0.8
#> 2 2024-01-01      0.6
om_campaigns("2015-01-25", "2018-01-25", every = "1 year",
             coverage = "@histITNcov@", by_year = TRUE)
#>         date         coverage
#> 1 2015-01-25 @histITNcov2015@
#> 2 2016-01-25 @histITNcov2016@
#> 3 2017-01-25 @histITNcov2017@
#> 4 2018-01-25 @histITNcov2018@

Define and deploy. define_OM_vector_control() writes the definition of the intervention and deploy_OM_vector_control() its deployment, with the same name and a schedule:

baseList = define_OM_vector_control(baseList, ig2, intervention_type = "ITN", name = "IG2")
schedule = om_campaigns(dates = c("2021-01-01", "2024-01-01"), coverage = c(0.8, 0.6))
baseList = deploy_OM_vector_control(baseList, "IG2", schedule)
  • Effects. Deterrency, pre-prandial and post-prandial killing become an OpenMalaria generic vector intervention (GVI). Each effect keeps its own decay; when attrition and insecticide decay cannot be expressed as a single OpenMalaria decay, a Weibull is fitted to their product, over 3 years for ITNs and 1 year for IRS (fit_years in om_vector_control()). When all decays are identical, the effects are written as a single component.
  • Exposure. The effects act on the mosquito populations exposed in bed (ITN) or resting indoors (IRS), see shares above (all bites without activity patterns, with a warning).
  • Same people. The deployment holds all the components of the intervention, so that all effects reach the same people.

Deployments restricted to age groups, and continuous deployment (e.g. EPI), are described in Age-specific deployments below.

What has been checked in OpenMalaria. The export was run in OpenMalaria through openMalariaUtilities and its entomological outputs checked (each effect on its own parameter, in the populations it should reach, decays, campaigns):

  • OpenMalaria 44: standard ITNs deployed by campaigns (also refresh on redeployment and baseline EIR);
  • OpenMalaria 49: standard ITNs (same effects as in 44), dummy-host nets (below), a list of nets with placeholder decays (identical to the nets defined separately), IRS (both IRS exposure definitions), age-restricted, cumulative and continuous deployments.

The plain-text route (get_OM_xml()) writes the same XML as the openMalariaUtilities route. Sub-population deployments have not been run in OpenMalaria.

Dummy-host nets. The GVI has deterrency and post-prandial killing only. Host-seeking killing, which the GVI cannot represent, is written as it is in the model, a dummy host on which every mosquito that finds it dies: for each campaign, an OpenMalaria non-human host (<name>_dummy_<k>, added at the campaign date), whose availability relative to an adult human is the coverage × KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute / human availability, and decays as the GVI effects do: attrition × insecticide decay of host-seeking killing, exact when it is a single OpenMalaria decay, otherwise the fitted Weibull (one modification with an increasing decay, none if it does not decay). As for the GVI, whose effects are refreshed (not stacked) in people who receive a net again, each campaign replaces the nets of its recipients: earlier dummy hosts are reduced by the coverage of every later campaign. In OpenMalaria 49, timing, coverage, replacement, populations reached and lifespan behave as designed, and the decay of the dummy hosts follows the written decay within 0.3% of the initial effect.

The relative availability of an added host is scaled by OpenMalaria by the availability of an average adult, the person sleeping in the experimental hut where host-seeking killing was measured. Relative to the average human of the population (the human of this package’s model), host-seeking killing is therefore stronger in OpenMalaria than in the package, by the ratio of adult to mean human availability (1.35 in the scenario checked, with a Tanzanian demography). This choice may be revisited.

Increasing decays need OpenMalaria schema 46 or later (checked with 49): set OMVersion = 49L in the baseList (or schema = 49 in get_OM_xml()); from schema 49, the entomology is written without propInfected / propInfectious, which 49 removed. Standard nets work with both 44 and 49.

The dummy hosts are written by deploy_OM_vector_control(), with the schedule. A dummy-host intervention is deployed once, with the whole schedule, and cannot be restricted to a sub-population, by age, or be cumulative. The hosts last until end_date if given (e.g. in om_campaigns()), otherwise 100 years:

ig2_dh = om_vector_control(get_ITN_params("Interceptor G2", "Kibondo",
                                          mode = "dummy_host", verbose = FALSE),
                           halflife_attrition = 2 * 365, shape_attrition = 2)
# baseList with OMVersion = 49L, set before define_OM_entomology()
baseList = define_OM_vector_control(baseList, ig2_dh, name = "IG2_dh")
schedule_dh = om_campaigns(dates = c("2021-01-01", "2024-01-01"), coverage = c(0.8, 0.6),
                           end_date = "2027-01-01")
baseList = deploy_OM_vector_control(baseList, "IG2_dh", schedule_dh)

Several nets. There are two cases:

  • Different nets in the same scenario (e.g. historical nets until 2018, then new nets): define and deploy each as its own intervention, with its own name and schedule.
  • Alternative nets across scenarios (e.g. to compare net types or trial parameterisations): a named list of interventions (same model structure) defines one intervention, deployed under the list’s name; in each scenario, one net of the list is used.

Placeholders only where something varies. The XML has numbers wherever the scenarios cannot differ, and placeholders elsewhere:

  • efficacies: placeholders with several nets;
  • decays: with decay = "placeholder" in define_OM_vector_control() (e.g. when the attrition varies between scenarios), otherwise the nets’ decays (which must then be the same). Each effect keeps its decay function when all the nets share it (e.g. a step for historical nets that last one year), and is otherwise a Weibull;
  • dummy hosts (dummy-host nets): availabilities as placeholders unless the net and the coverages are fixed; their decay (that of host-seeking killing, @<name>_hsk_L@ / _k@) as the other decays.

Here the built-in and the custom net as alternatives, with placeholder coverages and decays:

nets = list(IG2 = ig2, custom = custom)
schedule_ph = om_campaigns("2021-01-01", "2024-01-01", every = "3 years",
                           coverage = "@cov@", by_year = TRUE)
baseList = define_OM_vector_control(baseList, nets, name = "ITN", decay = "placeholder")
baseList = deploy_OM_vector_control(baseList, "ITN", schedule_ph)

Filling the scenario table. The scenario table is yours (built e.g. with expand.grid(), with your own coverages). om_scenario_values() adds to it, row by row, the values of the placeholders that were written: the efficacies of the net named in column net, the decays and, for dummy-host nets, the availabilities of the dummy hosts (from the coverage columns, named like the placeholders of the schedule). The source is the baseList (after define and deploy) or the result of get_OM_xml(), which keep what was written, so the values cannot disagree with the XML.

The decays differ between effects through the insecticide decay of each effect (from the trial parameterisation), while the attrition is the same for all effects. So by default halflife and kappa name one attrition column each (in years, decay_unit = "days" otherwise), and each effect’s decay is this attrition combined with its insecticide decay (the dummy hosts take the attrition as it is, their insecticide decay being separate; combine = FALSE writes final decays given per effect instead):

# Without openMalariaUtilities, the same definition and deployment as text
xml = get_OM_xml(om_ento, nets, schedule_ph, name = "ITN", decay = "placeholder",
                 entomology = FALSE)
scens = expand.grid(net = c("IG2", "custom"), attrition = c(2, 3),
                    cov2021 = c(0.5, 0.8), cov2024 = 0.6, seed = 1:2)
scens = om_scenario_values(scens, xml, net = "net", halflife = "attrition")
head(scens)
#>      net attrition cov2021 cov2024 seed ITN_deterrency ITN_preprandial
#> 1    IG2         2     0.5     0.6    1           0.71            0.44
#> 2 custom         2     0.5     0.6    1           0.40            0.50
#> 3    IG2         3     0.5     0.6    1           0.71            0.44
#> 4 custom         3     0.5     0.6    1           0.40            0.50
#> 5    IG2         2     0.8     0.6    1           0.71            0.44
#> 6 custom         2     0.8     0.6    1           0.40            0.50
#>   ITN_postprandial ITN_deterrency_L ITN_deterrency_k ITN_preprandial_L
#> 1             0.52          2.04272          2.05216           1.95368
#> 2             0.30          2.00000          2.00000           2.00000
#> 3             0.52          3.07923          2.11190           2.90807
#> 4             0.30          3.00000          2.00000           3.00000
#> 5             0.52          2.04272          2.05216           1.95368
#> 6             0.30          2.00000          2.00000           2.00000
#>   ITN_preprandial_k ITN_postprandial_L ITN_postprandial_k
#> 1           1.94825            1.90174            1.89557
#> 2           2.00000            2.00000            2.00000
#> 3           1.89938            2.79958            1.80697
#> 4           2.00000            3.00000            2.00000
#> 5           1.94825            1.90174            1.89557
#> 6           2.00000            2.00000            2.00000

Lower-level functions. define_OM_vector_control() is built on get_OM_GVI_snippet(), which returns the GVI as the input list of openMalariaUtilities’ defineVectorControl(), and add_OM_GVI(), which writes it into a baseList. They are useful to write the deployment yourself, e.g. with openMalariaUtilities’ deployIT(); in that case, deploy all components of an intervention together.

om_gvi = get_OM_GVI_snippet(ig2, om_ento, intervention_type = "ITN")
#> OpenMalaria export: Deterrency decay = Weibull fitted to attrition x insecticide decay (rmse 0.00117)
#> OpenMalaria export: PrePrandial decay = Weibull fitted to attrition x insecticide decay (rmse 0.00113)
#> OpenMalaria export: PostPrandial decay = Weibull fitted to attrition x insecticide decay (rmse 0.00225)
om_gvi[[1]]$deterrency$decay   # L in years
#> $L
#> [1] "2.04272"
#> 
#> $`function`
#> [1] "weibull"
#> 
#> $k
#> [1] "2.05216"

Without openMalariaUtilities (XML text)

get_OM_xml() writes the same entomology and interventions as XML text, to paste into an existing scenario:

  • entomology: the <vector> element (one <anopheles> per mosquito population, with its contribution as annualEIR and the seasonality placeholders "@m1@", …, "@m12@"), inside <entomology>, to which you add the total EIR as scaledAnnualEIR="@EIR@" (or a number);
  • define (the components) and deploy (the deployment): inside <interventions><human>, the components before all deployments;
  • add_hosts and modify_hosts, for dummy-host interventions (with schema = 49): the dummy hosts, inside <interventions><addNonHumanHosts>, and their decays, inside <interventions><nonHumanHostsModifications>.

schema (default 44) is the OpenMalaria schema version of the scenario.

Printing the result shows each snippet with a comment saying where it goes; writeLines(unlist(xml), "file.xml") saves them. get_OM_xml(om_ento) gives the entomology only; for several interventions, call it once per intervention with entomology = FALSE after the first.

schedule = om_campaigns("2021-01-01", "2024-01-01", every = "3 years",
                        coverage = "@cov@", by_year = TRUE)
xml = get_OM_xml(om_ento, ig2, schedule, name = "IG2")
#> OpenMalaria export: Deterrency decay = Weibull fitted to attrition x insecticide decay (rmse 0.00117)
#> OpenMalaria export: PrePrandial decay = Weibull fitted to attrition x insecticide decay (rmse 0.00113)
#> OpenMalaria export: PostPrandial decay = Weibull fitted to attrition x insecticide decay (rmse 0.00225)
cat(xml$deploy)
#> <deployment name="IG2">
#>   <component id="IG2-deterrency"/>
#>   <component id="IG2-preprandialKillingEffect"/>
#>   <component id="IG2-postprandialKillingEffect"/>
#>   <timed>
#>     <deploy coverage="@cov2021@" time="2021-01-01"/>
#>     <deploy coverage="@cov2024@" time="2024-01-01"/>
#>   </timed>
#> </deployment>

Age-specific deployments

Nets can be deployed to age groups in two ways:

  • campaigns restricted to an age group: at given dates, people of an age range receive the net (e.g. under-fives);
  • continuous deployment: people receive the net when they reach a target age (e.g. infants at 3 months through EPI), while the deployment is active.

Both take the same arguments in deploy_OM_vector_control() (openMalariaUtilities) and get_OM_xml() (text). They apply to standard interventions (dummy-host interventions are deployed to the whole population).

Campaigns for an age group. minAge and maxAge (in years, numbers or placeholders) restrict every campaign of the schedule to that age range; the coverage is then the coverage within the age group. Give both or neither: a single limit is an error, to avoid a deployment that silently reaches all ages. Here the IG2 net to under-fives, in 2021 and 2024:

baseList = define_OM_vector_control(baseList, ig2, name = "IG2")
schedule_u5 = om_campaigns(dates = c("2021-01-01", "2024-01-01"),
                           coverage = "@covU5@", by_year = TRUE)
baseList = deploy_OM_vector_control(baseList, "IG2", schedule_u5, minAge = 0, maxAge = 5)

The same deployment as text:

schedule_u5 = om_campaigns(dates = c("2021-01-01", "2024-01-01"),
                           coverage = "@covU5@", by_year = TRUE)
xml_u5 = get_OM_xml(om_ento, ig2, schedule_u5, name = "IG2",
                    minAge = 0, maxAge = 5, entomology = FALSE)
#> OpenMalaria export: Deterrency decay = Weibull fitted to attrition x insecticide decay (rmse 0.00117)
#> OpenMalaria export: PrePrandial decay = Weibull fitted to attrition x insecticide decay (rmse 0.00113)
#> OpenMalaria export: PostPrandial decay = Weibull fitted to attrition x insecticide decay (rmse 0.00225)
cat(xml_u5$deploy)
#> <deployment name="IG2">
#>   <component id="IG2-deterrency"/>
#>   <component id="IG2-preprandialKillingEffect"/>
#>   <component id="IG2-postprandialKillingEffect"/>
#>   <timed>
#>     <deploy coverage="@covU52021@" time="2021-01-01" minAge="0" maxAge="5"/>
#>     <deploy coverage="@covU52024@" time="2024-01-01" minAge="0" maxAge="5"/>
#>   </timed>
#> </deployment>

For several age groups, deploy the net once per group, each with its own schedule and coverage placeholders (in text: the define snippet once, the deploy snippet of each group). The age ranges should not overlap, otherwise people in both ranges receive a net from each deployment.

Continuous deployment. om_continuous() gives the target ages, the coverage at each age (numbers or placeholders) and, optionally, the dates between which the deployment is active (by default, from the start of the intervention period, without end). It is used as the schedule; campaign options (minAge, maxAge, cumulative, end_date) do not apply, but subpop does. Here nets to infants at 3 months (EPI), from 2021:

baseList = deploy_OM_vector_control(baseList, "IG2",
    om_continuous(age = 0.25, coverage = "@covEPI@", begin = "2021-01-01"))

The same deployment as text:

cont = om_continuous(age = 0.25, coverage = "@covEPI@", begin = "2021-01-01")
xml_cont = get_OM_xml(om_ento, ig2, cont, name = "IG2", entomology = FALSE)
#> OpenMalaria export: Deterrency decay = Weibull fitted to attrition x insecticide decay (rmse 0.00117)
#> OpenMalaria export: PrePrandial decay = Weibull fitted to attrition x insecticide decay (rmse 0.00113)
#> OpenMalaria export: PostPrandial decay = Weibull fitted to attrition x insecticide decay (rmse 0.00225)
cat(xml_cont$deploy)
#> <deployment name="IG2">
#>   <component id="IG2-deterrency"/>
#>   <component id="IG2-preprandialKillingEffect"/>
#>   <component id="IG2-postprandialKillingEffect"/>
#>   <continuous>
#>     <deploy coverage="@covEPI@" targetAgeYrs="0.25" begin="2021-01-01"/>
#>   </continuous>
#> </deployment>

Continuous and campaigns together. A net distributed both routinely and by mass campaigns is deployed twice under the same name, once with each schedule (two deployments of the same components); in text, call get_OM_xml() once per schedule and paste the define snippet of one call only.
